controls.Text: Processing mode
Film stock
Scan shows the reversal film directly, without a print stock. Print diffusion and scanner glare do not apply.
controls.TextInScan: Scan shows the simulated negative. Invert creates a linear positive that may need exposure adjustment. Use Print Simulation for a paper response.

controls.Label: Print stock
Options: fujifilm_crystal_archive_typeii = Fujifilm Crystal Archive Type II

controls.Label: Film exposure
controls.ToolTip: Light on the film. With Automatic film exposure on, the source is metered first and this is an offset from that. The print is timed for 0 EV, so more film exposure gives a denser negative and a brighter print; use Print exposure to bring brightness back while keeping the film's tone and grain.

controls.Label: Print exposure
controls.ToolTip: More light on the print stock makes the result darker.

controls.Text: Live Viewer · 8699 × 5809
This look uses sRGB input, which clips saturated colours before the film simulation. ProPhoto RGB keeps them.

controls.Label: Use recommended input
controls.ToolTip: Sets Input preparation to Neutral for film and Input color space to ProPhoto RGB for this look. The current look is saved as a version first, so you can restore it.

controls.Text: Viewer resolution

controls.Label: Viewer resolution
controls.ToolTip: Resolution of the final Viewer frame. Auto renders the size the image has on screen (1600–2560 px) and switches to native resolution when you zoom in; judge grain and sharpness zoomed in or at Native resolution. Save preview PNG saves the frame as shown. Viewer settings apply to all photos; they are not part of a look. Export does not use this setting.

controls.Text: Drag preview resolution

controls.Label: Drag preview resolution
controls.ToolTip: Temporary frame while dragging, and during other adjustments to large Viewer previews. Off disables temporary frames. Applies to all photos.

controls.Label: Automatic film exposure
controls.ToolTip: Meters the source to mid grey before exposing the film. Film exposure then acts as an offset, and brightness changes made in Capture One are largely metered away. Turn it off to expose the film directly from the Capture One image.

Renderer transport encoding (technical)

controls.ToolTip: Only changes how pixel values travel from the renderer to the panel. The panel decodes them back before display and export, so the look does not change. Leave it at sRGB.

Options: davinci_wide_gamut = DaVinci Wide Gamut / Intermediate (log; no ICC)
controls.ToolTip: Sets the exported profile. Viewer pixels remain sRGB before monitor correction; this is not a full wide-gamut soft proof. Output compression keeps sRGB; disable it to retain wider export colors. DaVinci Intermediate and V-Log exports carry no embedded profile.

controls.Text: TIFF and PNG retain 16-bit precision. JPEG is lossy 8-bit. Linear DNG uses Rec.2020 regardless of the selected profile.
Halation and scatter are off (amount 0). Raise an amount to enable the related controls.

controls.Label: Highlight boost (EV)
controls.ToolTip: Capture One delivers highlights clipped at white, so halation has little light to spread. Boost re-expands the brightest highlights before halation and scatter.

controls.Label: Highlight protection (EV)
controls.ToolTip: EV below the brightest highlight where Highlight boost starts. 1–2 EV boosts only the brightest areas.

controls.Label: Measure protection down from the brightest highlight
controls.ToolTip: On: Highlight boost acts on the top part of the image's brightness range; protection is how many EV below the brightest highlight it starts. Off: the original Spektrafilm rule, protection is EV above mid grey. Capture One images end at sensor clipping, usually only 2–3 EV above mid grey, so with the original rule and 4 EV protection the boost changes nothing. Native engine only; saved looks keep the original rule.

controls.Text: These three values are the renderer's "use film stock" marker, so the stock's own halation colour is still used. Move any slider to override it.
Filter
Select a filter to enable diffusion. Saved strength is retained while Off.
Filter
Select a filter to enable diffusion. Saved strength is retained while Off.
controls.TextInScan: Print diffusion requires a printing stage. Saved filter settings are retained.

controls.Text: Grain model is Off: the grain controls below have no effect until you choose a model. Film format still scales optical effects.
Grain model

Experimental model: Grain Synthesis can change brightness and color as well as texture. Use Production for more stable tones. Full-resolution preview/export supports up to 32 MP with Synthesis; saved quality settings are retained.

controls.Label: Keep average colour under grain
controls.ToolTip: Grain drawn per pixel shifts the average density and, through the print, the average colour; more so at higher resolutions (about 3–8% darker and cooler at 24 MP). On: the local average is restored to the grain-free image, so preview and export match and the colour no longer depends on resolution. Grain texture is kept; only its coarsest variation is slightly reduced. Off: the original Spektrafilm behaviour. Native engine only; saved looks keep their previous setting.

controls.Section: Spektrafilm optics › Spektrafilm grain › Grain synthesis
controls.Label: Match grain to output size
controls.ToolTip: On: each pixel averages the grain over its own area on the film, so a smaller preview or a downsized export keeps the average colour and grain of a downscaled full-size render. Full size from 24 MP and larger 35 mm files is unchanged. Off: the original behaviour, where smaller renders get darker, colour-shifted and much grainier. Native engine only; saved looks keep their previous setting.

controls.Section: Spektrafilm optics › Spektrafilm grain › Grain synthesis
controls.Label: Remove sampling noise
controls.ToolTip: On: when “Match grain to output size” enlarges the pixels (smaller previews, downsized exports, Draft synthesis preview), each pixel gets the grain strength of a render with unlimited samples, at the same render time. Full size from 24 MP and larger 35 mm files is unchanged. Off: the original behaviour, where fewer samples give stronger, noisier grain. Saved looks keep their previous setting.

controls.Section: Spektrafilm optics › Spektrafilm grain › Grain synthesis
controls.Label: Blur grain as light
controls.ToolTip: On: the final grain blur averages the light passing through the film, as a lens or scanner does, instead of averaging density. Colours under grain stay correct even without “Keep average colour under grain”, and the grain keeps the strength of the grain model; with that option on, grain is about a third weaker than with this one off. With “Match grain to output size” and “Remove sampling noise”, smaller previews and downsized exports get the grain of a downscaled full-size render. Off: the original density blur. Saved looks keep their previous setting.

controls.Text: Enable scanner controls to adjust scanning. Saved values are retained while disabled.

controls.Label: White point
controls.ToolTip: sRGB-coded level for the brightest print this film can make on this paper (Python Spektrafilm semantics). Mid-grey is kept by re-timing the print, so mainly the highlights move. In an inverted negative scan it applies to the film's clearest density.

controls.Label: Black point
controls.ToolTip: sRGB-coded level for the deepest print black this film can make on this paper (Python Spektrafilm semantics; 0.01 ≈ 3/255). Mid-grey is kept by re-timing the print, so mainly the shadows move. In an inverted negative scan it applies to the film's densest area.

controls.Label: Glare blur (px)
controls.ToolTip: Measured in output pixels, not on the film, so the same value looks wider on a small preview than on a full-resolution export.

controls.Label: Enlarger scale
controls.ToolTip: 1.0 keeps the original framing. Higher values magnify the image inside the frame.

controls.Text: Diffusion width is 0: couplers act without spatial spread, so Tail width and Tail weight have no effect.

controls.Label: Override stock coupler channels
controls.ToolTip: Off: each film uses its own measured coupler values. On: the sliders below replace them for every film; their defaults are generic, not the selected stock's values.

controls.Text:
Capture One's Export uses its active export recipes: location, file names, format (including PSD and PSB), ICC profile, size, metadata, watermark and output sharpening. The files are listed before the export starts, and an interrupted export can be resumed.
The panel's export buttons use the panel's settings instead: TIFF/PNG 16-bit or JPEG 8-bit in the selected export color space. Linear DNG uses Rec.2020 with highlight headroom. DaVinci Intermediate and V-Log are written without an embedded profile; tag the colour space in the receiving application. Selected variants keep their own saved settings; disabled variants use C1 development. Batch creates new filenames and retains completed files if canceled. Up to 100 MP / 16384 px per side; Native Grain Synthesis up to 32 MP.
Color-only LUTs map sRGB input to sRGB and include finishing color and tone. They exclude micro contrast, adaptive exposure, spatial effects and geometry, so they do not reproduce the complete Viewer look.
